messages:
Aria Chen: incident-bot just fired for JunoHealth dedicated pool 'jh-prod-d1' — paging increased 3x and toolcall parser errors showing repeated 'unexpected token' in tool response. stack shows parser v2.4.1 being used. Error rate 12% across that pool. Incident bot: SEV2 - toolcall-parser-regression (automated).
ops-bot: autopager triggered: queue depth > 1200, instance paging to disk. Autoscale attempted +2 but failed due to kernel OOM triggered on one node.
Sam Patel: I'm taking this. Oncall switching to me. @Marta can you confirm whether parser rollout happened last deploy?
Marta López: yes, parser v2.4.1 rolled in at 02:05 UTC in dedicated pools for customers flagged as 'parser-opt-in' — JunoHealth was opt-in per commit 9f3a. Rolling back now.
Aria Chen: customer impact: JunoHealth reports latency spikes (tail p95 > 6s) and 5% of toolcall responses malformed; affecting billing pipelines. CS notified (JunoHealth Oncall).
JunoHealth Oncall: we're seeing retries in our ingestion and duplicates — can you pause their traffic?
Sam Patel: initiating immediate mitigation: 1) route JunoHealth traffic away from jh-prod-d1 to warm fallback pool jh-prod-warm; 2) apply parser-compat shim that tolerates missing fields; 3) rollback parser to v2.3.8
Sam Patel: curl to switch routing (runbook):
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/route/switch \\
  -d '{"customer":"juno","from":"jh-prod-d1","to":"jh-prod-warm","drain":true}' \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```
Kevin O'Neill: I pushed the route switch. traffic draining, warm pool taking 30% extra. watch for cold-start tail latency.
ops-bot: route update success. Drain started on jh-prod-d1. Active connections 430 -> draining.
Marta López: rolling back parser via canary config:
```
kubectl set image deploy/parser parser=parser:2.3.8 -n dedicated-jh
```
Marta López: rollback completed on 3/4 nodes; one node failed due to OOM while restarting, I've removed it from rotation.
Sam Patel: monitoring metrics: toolcall error rate dropping from 12% -> 2.1% over 9 minutes. paging ops dropping to normal.
Aria Chen: alert: some requests still hitting old pool via regional routing; adding precise tag match to ensure all juno requests go to warm. @rotation-bot can we escalate to infra for kernel OOM followup?
rotation-bot: paging incident noted, assigned to Kevin for hardware-side investigation.
Kevin O'Neill: investigating node OOM — found an older kernel module sitting from earlier image; patching and reimaging node now. Will replace the failed node with new instance.
JunoHealth Oncall: thanks — can you confirm any data loss? We're seeing duplicates but no gaps.
Sam Patel: no data loss detected; duplicates are from retries. We're adding idempotency headers on proxy to suppress retries for 30m as mitigation.
Sam Patel: `headers: {X-Idempotency-Window: 1800}` added to routing proxy config.
ops-bot: config push succeeded.
Marta López: QA run on parser v2.3.8 completed; structured responses validated against juno schema. Marking as stable.
Aria Chen: customer-facing summary so far: brief timeline, cause (parser v2.4.1 schema stricter -> unexpected tokens -> parser exceptions -> increased CPU and KV cache churn -> paging), mitigations (routing to warm pool, rollback to v2.3.8, idempotency proxied, node replacement). CS to follow up with JunoHealth.
Sam Patel: action items:
- Kevin: finish node replacement + write postmortem section for kernel OOM (owner: Kevin)
- Marta: add parser rollout gating to ensure dedicated pools have compatibility tests (owner: Marta)
- Aria: update customer incident summary and coordinate postmortem with CS (owner: Aria)
- Sam: run canary test harness to simulate opt-in parser on dedicated pools (owner: Sam)
Sam Patel: handing off to next oncall @Marta for monitoring and postmortem. Last state: error rate stable at 0.9%, routing to warm pool, one node out for replacement.
Marta López: taking over. I'll update the incident channel and start the SEV2 postmortem doc.
Aria Chen: thanks team :thumbsup: 
ops-bot: incident SEV2 transitioned to 'stabilized' and handoff recorded.
